pending_interview.category: Martech/AI-product — personalization architecture, attribution modeling, GenAI content pipelines, measurement under privacy constraints
pending_interview.question: You are advising a large e-commerce brand that wants to build a real-time personalization engine — one that surfaces different product recommendations and homepage content to each user based on their behavior. Their data team has strong first-party behavioral data, but new privacy regulations in their primary markets have eliminated third-party cookie tracking and significantly restricted cross-site identity resolution. Their current attribution model (the method they use to figure out which marketing touchpoints actually caused a purchase) relies heavily on multi-touch attribution using that now-restricted data. Walk me through how you would redesign their personalization and attribution architecture under these constraints — what data sources and modeling approaches would you lean on, what would you deprioritize, and what tradeoffs would you make explicit to leadership?
